DECISIVE for the overturn: I enumerated every child tag inside every <reward> block — 131 <loot>, 131 <id>, 131 <qty>, 131 <chance>, 66 <reward>, and NOTHING ELSE. There is no scalar coin field anywhere in npcdata, so 'there is no scalar to seed' is proven, not asserted. REBUILD_READINESS.md:215 carries the ledger_text verbatim, including the backticked '=8'. OVERTURN UPHELD on the coins half: coins-per-kill is fully tabulated per NPC and the INFERRED '=8' seed has nothing to be a seed OF. TWO HONEST CAVEATS, neither refuting: (1) the credit function §1t6172s0§.as:847-854 applies 'param1 *= 1.5' under a timed-boost check, so the sum is a BASE that a buff scales — incompleteness, not error (see new finding s27e-nf-b); (2) the claim's own C2 build note is correct and correctly stated — npcdata.xml is android v0.682, the roll code is web v0.717. The gate is exact: :3050 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;', and :3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) { return; }' enforces it inside nextStance. FOCUS_MAX=192 is real: :249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;'. 48 = 192/4, four switches from full — arithmetic checks. The android numbers the claim warns against are also exactly right: MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' (=120) and :2977 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) { return; }' (=20), against MCSPlayer.as:3098-3104's two-branch debit. All four ledger cites resolve verbatim — SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:388 'Hard lock', :390 the exact quoted CONTRACT/CONTRADICTION row, :2099, and REBUILD_READINESS.md:158-160. OVERTURN UPHELD. And I found the mechanism that reconciles the frames rather than overriding them, which is stronger than what the claim argued: the web BattleUI stance button (§1t113s0§.as:468-479) and the SPACE key (§1t1541s0§.as:605-615) BOTH branch on §1t4470s0§() and play 'Snd_error' when it fails, and §1t99s0§.as:250 sets §1t4414s0§ = 0 at battle init — so a fight ALWAYS starts with 0/192 focus and the switch is ALWAYS unavailable at the instant a fight starts, which is precisely when the video study reports the 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' label appearing. No frame is being overridden here: the frame observation stands and the code explains it. What falls is the ledger's INFERENCE from that label ('hard lock', 'recreation only'). Corroborated independently by shs3_android/scripts/GameEngine.as:584 'str = "Tip: In battle, you can use spacebar to change stance.";'. One wording slop, not refutable: 'halve to maxreload/3' at MCSPlayer.as:3100 is a clamp to 40, not a halving. Note also that 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' appears in ZERO extracted artifacts — not in ui_strings.txt, not in strings.json — only in video-study prose.

Both halves verified, both by artifact. new_findings.text: The second half of RR:215 blocker ① — '20+ samples show no XP formula either' — is FALSE. The complete XP award function is in the web payload at §1t68s0§.as:185-209, and it is called on kill at :888 as §1t12070s0§(StatsManager.getLevel(), this.level, this.xp, false). The rule, read straight off the lines: award 0 if the enemy level is at or below a level-scaled floor (§1t12068s0§, :113-128: 0 below player level 6, then lvl - floor(lvl/10) - 5 under 40, lvl - floor(lvl/5) - 1 under 60, else lvl - 9); award 0 if the enemy is more than 3 levels above you (:191-193); otherwise base = enemy xp, scaled UP by (1 + 0.05 * levelGap) when the enemy out-levels you (:198) and DOWN by (1 - underGap / §1t12069s0§()) when you out-level it (:202, divisor 5 below player level 8, 6 below 10, 7 below 12, 8 below 16, ...), then doubled if the boolean flag is set (:204-206). The enemy's own xp is not a table lookup at all — it is closed-form: §1t68s0§.as:237 'this.xp = this.level * 2 + 20;' (same at :271). Nothing here needs measuring. This is why npcdata.xml carries ZERO <xp> tags (grep -c '<xp>' = 0) — there was never a per-NPC xp row to find, which is exactly the shape of evidence that made 20+ video samples look like 'no formula'.
new_findings.quote: §1t68s0§.as:191 'if(param2 - param1 > 3)' · :198 '_loc5_ = param3 * (1 + 0.05 * (param2 - param1));' · :202 '_loc5_ = param3 * (1 - (param1 - param2) / §1t12069s0§());' · :237 'this.xp = this.level * 2 + 20;'
new_findings.ledger_text: ① coins-per-kill reality (`=8` is an **unconfirmed INFERRED seed**; 20+ samples show no XP formula either).
new_findings.lane_impact: L4 economy / L2 progression: blocker ① dies completely rather than half. Ship XP_FROM_NPC(lvl) = lvl*2 + 20 and the award function as CONTRACT (web v0.717), including the two zero-award cutoffs — they are the anti-farm rules and a build without them will feel wrong at every level boundary.

new_findings.text: Coins-per-kill is a BASE that a buff scales, so the loot-table sum is not the whole payout. The credit function §1t6172s0§.as:847-854 — the §1t5846s0§ called at §1t68s0§.as:863 and :867 — opens with a boost check and multiplies the incoming amount by 1.5 before crediting. The check §1t1523s0§.§1t9725s0§ (§1t1523s0§.as:5011-5016) compares a stored expiry against a clock, i.e. it is a TIMED purchasable boost, and the constant passed is §1t9458s0§ = 6 (§1t1523s0§.as:338). This does not weaken the coins-per-kill overturn — it adds the multiplier layer that any faithful economy needs.
new_findings.lane_impact: L4 economy: COIN_BOOST_MULT = 1.5, boost id 6, timed. Applies to the credit, so it multiplies the loot-table sum, not each row.

new_findings.text: Two hard shapes of the drop system that the coins finding did not state. FIRST: only 66 of the 495 <npc> rows carry a <reward> block at all — 429 enemies drop NOTHING. Measured by streaming every <reward>...</reward> block and histogramming its children: 66 <reward>, 131 <loot>, 131 <id>, 131 <qty>, 131 <chance>, no other tag. SECOND: the roll's switch is not closed at 3. §1t68s0§.as:877-879 is an ELSE branch calling §1t6186s0§(_loc7_, _loc8_) — loot id passed straight through as an ITEM CODE with a quantity — and npcdata does use it: the 131 rows break down as id 0 x77 (1 coin each), id 1 x10 (5 coins each), id 2 x10 (§1t6183s0§, no args), id 3 x28 (§1t6194s0§(this.level,false,true), level-scaled), plus ids 2112 x2, 2113 x2, 2114 x1 and 20028 x1, which fall to the item branch.

new_findings.lane_impact: L4 economy: do not give every mob a drop. 429/495 drop nothing; the loot id is a UNION (0-3 are currency/special, anything else is an item code), so the seeded table needs a fallthrough, not a 4-way enum.

new_findings.text: The frame observation and the web code do not actually conflict, and the reconciliation is in the artifacts. Both web input paths into the stance switch branch on the same 48-focus predicate and FAIL AUDIBLY rather than being absent: the BattleUI stance button (§1t113s0§.as:468-479) plays 'Snd_smallClick' and calls nextStance when §1t4470s0§() holds, else plays 'Snd_error'; the SPACE key (§1t1541s0§.as:605-615) does the identical two-branch thing. And §1t99s0§.as:250 sets the focus meter to 0 at battle init, so a fight ALWAYS opens at 0/192 with the switch unavailable — exactly the moment the video study reports the label appearing. So 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' is the unavailable-state readout of a gate, not the absence of a mechanic. Independent corroboration that switching in battle exists at all: shs3_android/scripts/GameEngine.as:584 is an in-game tip that says so in plain English. Note also that the string 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' occurs in ZERO extracted artifacts — absent from reference/extracted/ui_strings.txt and from the 2,533-entry strings.json — it survives only in video-study prose, so no artifact currently pins its exact trigger. THE FRAME IS NOT BEING OVERRIDDEN HERE: the label is real and stays; what falls is the inference drawn from it.

new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud: the stance label is a two-state readout driven by the SAME predicate as the button (canChangeStance && focus >= 48), and a failed press must play the error SFX, not do nothing. That is a shippable HUD contract, and it is what makes the video frames and the code agree.

new_findings.text: A measured, first-hand web-vs-android divergence in the SAME meter, which is the cleanest counterexample I found to treating the android decompile as a stand-in for v0.717. The web player initialises its focus maximum to 8 * 24 = 192 with the current value at 0; the android twin initialises maxreload to 5 * 24 = 120 with reload at 0. Same function position, same init sequence (both immediately followed by the HUD update call), different constant. Every ratio-based port between the two builds must be rescaled by 192/120, and the web's stance toll of 48 is 25% of the bar while the android's threshold of maxreload/6 = 20 is 16.7% of its own.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: FOCUS_MAX = 192 CONTRACT (web v0.717). Concrete evidence for the C2 caveat — the builds differ on tuning constants even where the code shape is identical.

new_findings.text: RR:155-156 says only 'Heavy's reach also scales', and the mastery finding repeats that framing. The reach switch says otherwise. §1t99s0§.as:3093-3094 gives Light a FLAT 1.4x reach; :3105 gives Balanced (1 + 0.2 * §1t4422s0§ * 0.1) = 1 + 0.02m, i.e. Balanced reach scales exactly like Balanced damage; :3116 gives Heavy (0.5 + 0.04m); :3142 gives Dual the unscaled base. Note the reach mapping is the MIRROR of the damage mapping — the stance that takes 0.5+0.04m on damage (:3262) takes 1.4 flat on reach, and vice versa — which is what makes Light long-and-weak and Heavy short-and-strong, consistent with the ledger's own 300/200/100 reach ordering. And every branch is clamped: :3117-3119 and the identical guards at :3143-3146 force the result up to 100 if it lands below, so a low-mastery Heavy does not reach below the floor.
new_findings.ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.** A level-1 Shugyosha does Light ×0.5 / Balanced ×1.0 / Heavy ×1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's *reach* also scales ×0.5→×0.9.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: ship FOUR reach rules, not one — STANCE_REACH_LIGHT = 1.4 flat, STANCE_REACH_BALANCED(m) = 1 + 0.02m, STANCE_REACH_HEAVY(m) = 0.5 + 0.04m, STANCE_REACH_DUAL = 1.0 — all applied to the weapon base and then clamped up to REACH_FLOOR = 100.

new_findings.text: The 1.3x multiplier that the ledger discusses as a crit is not rolled — it is a full-meter condition, deterministic. The damage function's tail at §1t99s0§.as:3272-3274 tests focus == maxfocus and returns the stanced damage times 1.3 plus a flat bonus term. No Math.random anywhere in that branch. Combined with the 48-per-switch toll (:3162) and the slash costs (:3302-3310) this makes Focus a single resource with a sharp cliff at the top: the bonus exists ONLY at exactly 192/192, so any spend at all removes it, and the same full-bar condition gates two other abilities (:3383, :3707). That is a very different feel from a percentage crit chance and would be trivially wrong to seed as one.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: CRIT_MULT = 1.3 is CONDITIONAL on a full 192/192 Focus bar, not probabilistic. Also explains why 20+ video samples never yielded a crit RATE — there isn't one.

new_findings.text: The coins finding names REBUILD_READINESS.md:215 but not the OTHER ledger row asserting the same thing, which is graded [CONTRACT] and marked '(verified)' — a stronger claim than the RR blocker and equally dead. SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:2098 resolves the '+5 vs +8' dispute in favour of +8 and calls it verified. There is no per-kill coin constant in the build: the credit is the loot-table sum (§1t68s0§.as:861-867, 1x per qty on id 0 and 5x per qty on id 1), the rows live per-NPC in npcdata's <reward> blocks, and 429 of 495 npcs have no <reward> at all so their coin yield is ZERO, not 8. The '+5' half of the dispute is very likely the 5x id-1 multiplier seen in isolation.
